summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 1.3/14)

data.turoyo: W u yawmo du ṭlobo kmawbəli aʕmayye qaḏ̣ame, meqəm hənne mqalanwola, maḥ ḥəmṣe, mqalanwola bu bayto, <...>
data.translation: Am Tag der Verlobung bringen sie qaḏ̣āme mit. Früher pflegten sie sie (selbst) zu rösten, aus Kichererbsen, die sie zu Hause rösteten, <...>

rationale: New Infectum-wa box: repeated past customary roasting, two tokens in one context.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 2.12/3)

data.turoyo: W mqalanwulle ʕam zayto, ya ʕam dəhniṯo, hawxa falqe falqe daq qarʕe, bəṯr mḥaḏ̣riwo u ḥašwayḏa.
data.translation: Sie pflegten sie mit Öl zu braten, oder mit Fett, die einzelnen Kürbisstücke. Dann bereiteten sie eine Füllung für sie zu: <...>

rationale: New Infectum-wa box: ʕam-marked cooking medium and suffixed pumpkin patient.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 2.7/16)

data.turoyo: U ḥa ... uxliwunne, u ḥa d obəʕ ste šəlaq... mqalewolən bab beʕe, <...>
data.translation: Wer .... man aß sie, aber wer wollte, der koch... der briet sie mit Eiern. <...>

rationale: New Infectum-wa box: source’s spoken repair retained; eggs expressed with b-.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 5.4/2)

data.turoyo: huwe faqiro i nuqro gabayye bi ləġa da qriyawoṯo ṭaġno mani d gəmqalenawo u məšḥo w saymina beʕe, <...>
data.translation: Der Arme, bei ihnen, im Dialekt der Dörfer, bedeutet nuqro eine Pfanne, eine in der wir Butterschmalz erhitzten und Eier darin brieten. <...>

rationale: New Infectum-wa box and participant extension: cooking fat itself is the direct material heated.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 2.10/3)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr kəmqalət baṣle ġalabe, bu zayto, hul d hawxa dowən karamel, kmaḥtət ab baṣlanək ʕəl mənayye w u zayto, ġalabe basimo kowən, <...>
data.translation: Dann brätst du viele Zwiebeln in Öl an, bis sie glasiert sind, und gibst diese Zwiebeln und das Öl darüber, dann wird die (mǧad́ dăra) sehr wohl- schmeckend. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: generic second person, zero-marked onions and b-marked oil.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 2.4/4)

data.turoyo: Čike mbašlinale, čike mqalenale, əšmənto d bošəl <...>
data.translation: Wir kochten (die Füllung) ein bisschen, wir brieten sie leicht an, bis sie etwas gar wurde. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: coordinated cooking/frying with object suffix; no new lightly-fry sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE interview 1/62)

data.turoyo: Harke kosaymina qawite, muqḏina bi+ṣaymənto Xədəlyás, muqḏina aḥ+ḥeṭe bu+dawqo, mqalínanne, ŭ gursínanne, ŭ matrínanne bam+maye ḥalye, bəṯr maḥtina dibəs aʕlayye, layšínanne, saymina i+qawite di+Xədəlyase, <...>
data.translation: Here we make kavut, we burn it during the Hıdırellez fast, we burn wheat in a skillet, we roast them, and we grind them, and we moisten them with sweet water, then we put grape molasses on them, we knead them, we make Hıdırellez kavut, <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: plural wheat patient and roasting in a complete preparation sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (75/84)

data.turoyo: Hul d hayo koḥəšwo ga yatiwo yo, mqalela ab beʕe, nafiqo huuu! Komaṭi lu gabo ḥreno du šalwo!
data.translation: Derweilen denkt sie: er sitzt noch da. Als sie die Eier gebraten hat und herauskommt, huu! Da ist er schon auf der anderen Seite des Tales angekommen.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: completion of frying precedes emergence from the cave.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (96/229)

data.turoyo: kit tloṯo taxtat ebe. Kit tloṯ ṣweni d rezo w tloṯ qaze maqalye aʕlayye.
data.translation: Darin standen drei Betten, und es waren drei Speiseplatten damit reis, und darauf drei gebratene Gänse.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell: plural food state maqalye.

summary: The evidence remains II braten, rösten throughout food preparation: onions, chickpeas, pumpkin, meat filling, wheat, eggs and poultry. Degree words such as čike do not create separate lexical senses.

Infectum-wa has mqalan-/mqalen- and mqalewo- variants, patient suffixes and customary-past contexts. Cooking medium occurs with b- (oil/eggs) or ʕam (oil/fat); patient agreement may follow a collective referent rather than the overt plural food pieces.
Detransitive Part. Pass. names the cooked result, including plural maqalye. Existing English examples are retained unchanged; new JTM and Ritter examples retain their own German translations.

The inherited request to verify Syriac etymology remains unresolved: this bounded textual input cannot establish a donor language. Isolated koqəlyo in 113/199 is excluded from the frying paradigm pending textual/root verification.
Does gəmqalenawo u məšḥo (JTM 5.4/2) mean heating fat itself, or describe frying through its medium? No browning or clarification of butter is attested here.
Confirm antecedents and segmentation of mqalanwola and mqalanwulle; feminine collective and masculine/collective reference should not be inferred solely from German number.
Is baṣro, baṣle (JTM 2.11/5) a spoken correction from meat to onions? Both remain unchanged in the source.
In 76/56, does ko- on kosimola scope over mqalyola and maḥtola for box filing? Each following verb lacks its own ko-.
Verify koqəlyo at 113/199 against the edition and its root/paradigm. The supplied alignment warning notes added names and a garbled tuft/prince clause; no translation from this verse is quoted.
Resolve the inherited etymology question from appropriate comparative sources in a separate editorial review.
Cooking fat can itself be the direct object in gəmqalenawo u məšḥo, rather than a b-/ʕam-marked medium. This does not establish a specialised technical heating sense.
